rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal performance. This test will evaluate combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, clarifying whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines. It directly addresses the core hypothesis of the study with minimal complexity, providing critical initial insights into modality interaction.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5265 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategies. It is a logical extension of the current setup and addresses a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal additional complexity, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (a key design choice not yet evaluated) with avgpool aggregation (a common alternative to None) and concat fusion (similar to the best-performing singleprofile setup). It clarifies whether multiprofile settings can improve performance and whether aggregation matters, balancing exploration of critical design decisions with incremental progress.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile settings (config_018) significantly outperform singleprofile. This experiment tests whether using a more powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) instead of resnet50 can further improve performance on multiprofile data with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion. This clarifies the impact of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, while building on the strong foundation of multiprofile settings.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile settings (config_018, 0.6186 accuracy; config_024, 0.6287 accuracy) outperform singleprofile configurations. These top performers use pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) in this high-performing configuration improves accuracy. It directly addresses the importance of fusion strategy in multimodal multiprofile settings, a critical design choice with sparse evidence yet.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_025) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex encoder) maintains or improves performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing pattern with exploration of a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_025: 0.6352). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex encoder) while maintaining the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion strategy could improve performance. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision with sparse evidence, and builds on the promising multiprofile/imagenet_vit_l direction.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_037) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while maintaining weighted fusion could further improve performance. It directly addresses the importance of aggregation methods in multimodal models with these encoders, providing critical insights without repeating prior configurations.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests the impact of fusion type (concat vs weighted) with the same RNA/image encoders and transformer aggregation, clarifying whether the fusion method is critical. It balances exploitation of proven components (scvi_n200, transformer) with exploration of fusion strategies, providing actionable insights without repeating prior configurations.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests replacing scvi_n200 RNA encoder with scgpt in the same setup, clarifying whether scgpt offers better performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about RNA encoder choice while building on a promising configuration.
